bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# xh

xh is a command-line HTTP client for sending and inspecting HTTP requests. It provides a friendly, concise interface for making HTTP requests and examining responses.

Usage

  xh [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...

Examples

  # Send a GET request
  xh http://example.org/json

  # Send a POST request with JSON-like key/value items
  xh http://example.org/post name=alice age:=30

  # Read the request body from stdin
  echo "[1,2,3]" | xh post http://example.org/post

Installation

Prebuilt binaries are available on the project's releases page:
https://github.com/ducaale/xh/releases

Alternatively, install using your system's package manager if available (e.g. Homebrew, apt, pacman, etc.).

For more detailed usage run:

  xh help

---BAK---
# xh
[![Version info](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/xh.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/xh)
[![Packaging status](https://repology.org/badge/tiny-repos/xh.svg)](https://repology.org/project/xh/versions)

`xh` is a friendly and fast tool for sending HTTP requests. It reimplements as much
as possible of [HTTPie's](https://httpie.io/) excellent design, with a focus
on improved performance.

[![asciicast](/assets/xh-demo.gif)](https://asciinema.org/a/475190)

## Installation

### via cURL (Linux & macOS)

```
curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ducaale/xh/master/install.sh | sh
```

### via Powershell (Windows)

```
iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ducaale/xh/master/install.ps1 | iex
```


### via a package manager

| OS                            | Method     | Command                                    |
|-------------------------------|------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Any                           | Cargo\*    | `cargo install xh --locked`                |
| Any                           | [Huber]    | `huber install xh`                         |
| Android ([Termux])            | pkg        | `pkg install xh`                           |
| Android ([Magisk]/[KernelSU]) | MMRL\*\*   | `mmrl install xhhttp`                      |
| Alpine Linux                  | apk\*\*\*  | `apk add xh`                               |
| Arch Linux                    | Pacman     | `pacman -S xh`                             |
| Debian & Ubuntu               | Apt\*\*\*\*| `sudo apt install xh`                      |
| FreeBSD                       | FreshPorts | `pkg install xh`                           |
| NetBSD                        | pkgsrc     | `pkgin install xh`                         |
| Linux & macOS                 | Nixpkgs    | `nix-env -iA nixpkgs.xh`                   |
| Linux & macOS                 | [Flox]     | `flox install xh`                          |
| Linux & macOS                 | Homebrew   | `brew install xh`                          |
| Linux & macOS                 | [Hermit]   | `hermit install xh`                        |
| macOS                         | MacPorts   | `sudo port install xh`                     |
| Windows                       | Scoop      | `scoop install xh`                         |
| Windows                       | Chocolatey | `choco install xh`                         |
| Windows                       | Winget     | `winget add ducaale.xh`                    |

\* Make sure that you have Rust 1.83 or later installed

\*\* You will need to install the [MMRL CLI](https://github.com/DerGoogler/MMRL-CLI/releases)

\*\*\* Built with native-tls only.

\*\*\*\* Available since Debian 13 and Ubuntu 25.04. Built with native-tls only.

[Huber]: https://github.com/innobead/huber#installing-huber
[Magisk]: https://github.com/topjohnwu/Magisk
[KernelSU]: https://kernelsu.org
[Termux]: https://github.com/termux/termux-app
[Flox]: https://flox.dev/docs/
[Hermit]: https://cashapp.github.io/hermit/

### via pre-built binaries
The [release page](https://github.com/ducaale/xh/releases) contains prebuilt binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Usage
```
Usage: xh [OPTIONS] <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...

Arguments:
  <[METHOD] URL>     The request URL, preceded by an optional HTTP method
  [REQUEST_ITEM]...  Optional key-value pairs to be included in the request.

Options:
  -j, --json                             (default) Serialize data items from the command line as a JSON object
  -f, --form                             Serialize data items from the command line as form fields
      --multipart                        Like --form, but force a multipart/form-data request even without files
      --raw <RAW>                        Pass raw request data without extra processing
      --pretty <STYLE>                   Controls output processing [possible values: all, colors, format, none]
      --format-options <FORMAT_OPTIONS>  Set output formatting options
  -s, --style <THEME>                    Output coloring style [possible values: auto, solarized, monokai, fruity]
      --response-charset <ENCODING>      Override the response encoding for terminal display purposes
      --response-mime <MIME_TYPE>        Override the response mime type for coloring and formatting for the terminal
  -p, --print <FORMAT>                   String specifying what the output should contain
  -h, --headers                          Print only the response headers. Shortcut for --print=h
  -b, --body                             Print only the response body. Shortcut for --print=b
  -m, --meta                             Print only the response metadata. Shortcut for --print=m
  -v, --verbose...                       Print the whole request as well as the response
      --debug                            Print full error stack traces and debug log messages
      --all                              Show any intermediary requests/responses while following redirects with --follow
  -P, --history-print <FORMAT>           The same as --print but applies only to intermediary requests/responses
  -q, --quiet...                         Do not print to stdout or stderr
  -S, --stream                           Always stream the response body
  -x, --compress...                      Content compressed (encoded) with Deflate algorithm
  -o, --output <FILE>                    Save output to FILE instead of stdout
  -d, --download                         Download the body to a file instead of printing it
  -c, --continue                         Resume an interrupted download. Requires --download and --output
      --session <FILE>                   Create, or reuse and update a session
      --session-read-only <FILE>         Create or read a session without updating it from the request/response exchange
  -A, --auth-type <AUTH_TYPE>            Specify the auth mechanism [possible values: basic, bearer, digest]
</output>

Run `xh help` for more detailed information.

### Request Items

`xh` uses [HTTPie's request-item syntax](https://httpie.io/docs/cli/request-items) to set headers, request body, query string, etc.

- `=`/`:=` for setting the request body's JSON or form fields (`=` for strings and `:=` for other JSON types).
- `==` for adding query strings.
- `@` for including files in multipart requests e.g `picture@hello.jpg` or `picture@hello.jpg;type=image/jpeg;filename=goodbye.jpg`.
- `:` for adding or removing headers e.g `connection:keep-alive` or `connection:`.
- `;` for including headers with empty values e.g `header-without-value;`.

An `@` prefix can be used to read a value from a file. For example: `x-api-key:@api-key.txt`.

The request body can also be read from standard input, or from a file using `@filename`.

To construct a complex JSON object, a JSON path can be used as a key e.g `app[container][0][id]=090-5`.
For more information on this syntax, refer to https://httpie.io/docs/cli/nested-json.

### Shorthand form for URLs

Similar to HTTPie, specifying the scheme portion of the request URL is optional, and a leading colon works as shorthand
for localhost. `:8000` is equivalent to `localhost:8000`, and `:/path` is equivalent to `localhost/path`.

URLs can have a leading `://` which allows quickly converting a URL into a valid xh or HTTPie command. For example
`http://httpbin.org/json` becomes `http ://httpbin.org/json`.


```sh
xh http://localhost:3000/users # resolves to http://localhost:3000/users
xh localhost:3000/users        # resolves to http://localhost:3000/users
xh :3000/users                 # resolves to http://localhost:3000/users
xh :/users                     # resolves to http://localhost:80/users
xh example.com                 # resolves to http://example.com
xh ://example.com              # resolves to http://example.com
```

### Making HTTPS requests by default

`xh` will default to HTTPS scheme if the binary name is one of `xhs`, `https`, or `xhttps`. If you have installed `xh`
via a package manager, both `xh` and `xhs` should be available by default. Otherwise, you need to create one like this:

```sh
cd /path/to/xh && ln -s ./xh ./xhs
xh httpbin.org/get  # resolves to http://httpbin.org/get
xhs httpbin.org/get # resolves to https://httpbin.org/get
```

### Strict compatibility mode

If `xh` is invoked as `http` or `https` (by renaming the binary), or if the `XH_HTTPIE_COMPAT_MODE` environment variable is set,
it will run in HTTPie compatibility mode. The only current difference is that `--check-status` is not enabled by default.

## Examples

```sh
# Send a GET request
xh httpbin.org/json

# Send a POST request with body {"name": "ahmed", "age": 24}
xh httpbin.org/post name=ahmed age:=24

# Send a GET request with querystring id=5&sort=true
xh get httpbin.org/json id==5 sort==true

# Send a GET request and include a header named x-api-key with value 12345
xh get httpbin.org/json x-api-key:12345

# Send a POST request with body read from stdin.
echo "[1, 2, 3]" | xh post httpbin.org/post

# Send a PUT request and pipe the result to less
xh put httpbin.org/put id:=49 age:=25 | less

# Download and save to res.json
xh -d httpbin.org/json -o res.json

# Make a request with a custom user agent
xh httpbin.org/get user-agent:foobar
```

## How xh compares to HTTPie

### Advantages

- Improved startup speed.
- Available as a single statically linked binary that's easy to install and carry around.
- HTTP/2 support.
- Builtin translation to curl commands with the `--curl` flag.
- Short, cheatsheet-style output from `--help`. (For longer output, pass `help`.)

### Disadvantages

- Not all of HTTPie's features are implemented. ([#4](https://github.com/ducaale/xh/issues/4))
- No plugin system.
- General immaturity. HTTPie is old and well-tested.
- Worse documentation.

## Similar or related Projects

- [curlie](https://github.com/rs/curlie) - frontend to cURL that adds the ease of use of httpie
- [httpie-go](https://github.com/nojima/httpie-go) - httpie-like HTTP client written in Go
- [curl2httpie](https://github.com/dcb9/curl2httpie) - convert command arguments between cURL and HTTPie

SHORT_TO_LONG = {}
for long, (short, _, _, _) in OPTION_DEFS.items():
    if short:
        SHORT_TO_LONG[short] = long


def set_arg(args, long, value):
    short, takes_value, dest, is_multi = OPTION_DEFS[long]
    if long in VALID_VALUES and value is not None:
        if value not in VALID_VALUES[long]:
            eprint(f"error: invalid value '{value}' for '--{long} <{long.upper()}>'")
            eprint(f"  [possible values: {', '.join(VALID_VALUES[long])}]")
            eprint()
            eprint(f"For more information, try '--help'.")
            sys.exit(2)
    if is_multi is True:
        lst = getattr(args, dest)
        lst.append(value)
    elif is_multi == "count":
        setattr(args, dest, getattr(args, dest) + 1)
    else:
        # boolean toggles or values
        if takes_value:
            setattr(args, dest, value)
        else:
            setattr(args, dest, True)
    # Handle --json/--form/--multipart as mutually exclusive (latest wins)
    if long == "json":
        args.form = False
        args.multipart = False
        args.json = True
    elif long == "form":
        args.json = False
        args.multipart = False
        args.form = True
    elif long == "multipart":
        args.json = False
        args.form = False
        args.multipart = True


def reset_arg(args, long):
    if long not in OPTION_DEFS:
        return False
    short, takes_value, dest, is_multi = OPTION_DEFS[long]
    if is_multi is True:
        setattr(args, dest, [])
    elif is_multi == "count":
        setattr(args, dest, 0)
    else:
        if takes_value:
            setattr(args, dest, None)
        else:
            setattr(args, dest, False)
    return True


def parse_args(argv):
    args = Args()
    positional = []
    i = 1
    n = len(argv)
    while i < n:
        a = argv[i]
        if a == "--":
            # Everything after is positional
            positional.extend(argv[i+1:])
            break
        if a == "--help":
            sys.stdout.write(short_help())
            sys.exit(0)
        if a in ("-V", "--version"):
            print_version()
            sys.exit(0)
        # --no-<opt> resets to default
        if a.startswith("--no-"):
            name = a[5:]
            if reset_arg(args, name):
                i += 1
                continue
            else:
                eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found")
                eprint()
                eprint(usage_line())
                eprint()
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
        if a.startswith("--"):
            # Can be --opt or --opt=val
            if "=" in a:
                key, val = a[2:].split("=", 1)
            else:
                key = a[2:]
                val = None
            if key not in OPTION_DEFS:
                eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found")
                eprint()
                eprint("  tip: to pass '{}' as a value, use '-- {}'".format(a, a))
                eprint()
                eprint(usage_line())
                eprint()
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            short, takes_value, dest, is_multi = OPTION_DEFS[key]
            if takes_value:
                if val is None:
                    if i + 1 >= n:
                        vals = VALID_VALUES.get(key)
                        msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{key} <{key.upper().replace('-','_')}>' but none was supplied"
                        eprint(msg)
                        if vals:
                            eprint(f"  [possible values: {', '.join(vals)}]")
                        eprint()
                        eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                        sys.exit(2)
                    val = argv[i+1]
                    i += 1
            else:
                if val is not None:
                    eprint(f"error: unexpected value '{val}' for '--{key}' found; no more were expected")
                    eprint()
                    eprint(usage_line())
                    eprint()
                    eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
            set_arg(args, key, val)
            i += 1
            continue
        if a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1 and not _is_negative_number(a):
            # Short option(s): -abc or -abvalue
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                ch = a[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_TO_LONG:
                    eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '-{ch}' found")
                    eprint()
                    eprint(usage_line())
                    eprint()
                    eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
                long = SHORT_TO_LONG[ch]
                short, takes_value, dest, is_multi = OPTION_DEFS[long]
                if takes_value:
                    # Rest of arg is value; else next arg
                    rest = a[j+1:]
                    if rest:
                        val = rest
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= n:
                            eprint(f"error: a value is required for '-{ch}' but none was supplied")
                            eprint()
                            eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                            sys.exit(2)
                        val = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                    set_arg(args, long, val)
                    break
                else:
                    set_arg(args, long, None)
                    j += 1
            i += 1
            continue
        # Positional
        positional.append(a)
        i += 1

    # Parse positional args
    if not positional:
        eprint("error: the following required arguments were not provided:")
        eprint("  <[METHOD] URL>")
        eprint()
        eprint(f"Usage: {PROG_NAME} <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...")
        eprint()
        eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
        sys.exit(2)

    # Handle 'help' subcommand-ish
    if positional[0] == "help" and len(positional) == 1:
        # Long help - just print short for now
        sys.stdout.write(short_help())
        sys.exit(0)

    # Determine method/URL
    first = positional[0]
    if len(positional) == 1:
        # Only one positional - it's URL (check if it's a valid URL or method-like)
        if is_method_like(first):
            # Looks like a method only
            make_error("Missing <URL>")
        args.method = None
        args.url = first
        rest = []
    else:
        if is_method_like(first):
            args.method = first.upper()
            args.url = positional[1]
            rest = positional[2:]
        else:
            args.method = None
            args.url = first
            rest = positional[1:]

    args.items = rest
    return args


def _is_negative_number(s):
    """Check if argument is a negative number (e.g. '-1'), not a flag."""
    if len(s) < 2 or s[0] != '-':
        return False
    return all(c.isdigit() or c == '.' for c in s[1:])


def normalize_url(url, https=False):
    """Normalize xh-style URL to proper URL.
    
    Rules:
    - Starts with http:// or https:// -> use as-is
    - Starts with ://  -> strip and prepend scheme
    - Starts with :PORT or :/ -> prepend localhost
    - Otherwise prepend scheme
    """
    scheme = "https" if https else "http"
    if url.startswith("://"):
        url = scheme + url
    elif url.startswith("http://") or url.startswith("https://"):
        pass
    elif url.startswith(":"):
        # localhost shorthand
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest == "" or rest.startswith("/"):
            # :/path -> localhost/path (but ":" alone is localhost:/)
            url = f"{scheme}://localhost{rest}"
        else:
            # :PORT/path -> localhost:PORT/path
            url = f"{scheme}://localhost:{rest}"
    else:
        url = f"{scheme}://{url}"
    return url


def parse_request_items(items, mode):
    """Parse items like key=val, key:=val, key==val, key:val, key;, file@path.
    
    mode: 'json', 'form', 'multipart'
    Returns:
      headers (list of (key, val) pairs; None val means unset)
      body_items (list of dicts)
      query_items (list of (key, val))
      files (for multipart)
    """
    headers = []
    body = []  # list of (key, value, type) where type in 'str','json','raw'
    query = []
    files = []  # list of (name, path, filename, mimetype)
    
    def unescape(s):
        # Handle escape sequences like \: or \= 
        out = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(s):
            if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s):
                out.append(s[i+1])
                i += 2
            else:
                out.append(s[i])
                i += 1
        return ''.join(out)
    
    # Find unescaped separator - longer sep first
    SEPS = [':=@', ':=', '==', '=@', '@', '=', ':', ';']
    
    for item in items:
        # Find earliest unescaped separator, preferring longer
        best_idx = None
        best_sep = None
        i = 0
        while i < len(item):
            if item[i] == '\\':
                i += 2
                continue
            for sep in SEPS:
                if item[i:i+len(sep)] == sep:
                    if best_idx is None or i < best_idx or (i == best_idx and len(sep) > len(best_sep)):
                        best_idx = i
                        best_sep = sep
                    break
            i += 1
        
        if best_idx is None:
            # No separator
            eprint(f"error: \"{item}\" is not a valid request item")
            sys.exit(2)
        
        key = unescape(item[:best_idx])
        val = item[best_idx + len(best_sep):]
        
        sep = best_sep
        # @ prefix in value means read from file
        if sep in (':=', '=', ':', 'header'):
            if val.startswith('@'):
                path = val[1:]
                try:
                    with open(path, 'r') as f:
                        val = f.read()
                except OSError as e:
                    eprint(f"error: cannot open file '{path}': {e}")
                    sys.exit(2)
        
        if sep == ':=':
            # JSON value
            try:
                parsed = jsonlib.loads(val)
            except Exception:
                eprint(f"error: \"{item}\" is not a valid request item")
                sys.exit(2)
            body.append((key, parsed, 'json'))
        elif sep == '==':
            query.append((key, val))
        elif sep == '=':
            body.append((key, val, 'str'))
        elif sep == ':':
            if val == '':
                headers.append((key, None))  # unset
            else:
                headers.append((key, val))
        elif sep == ';':
            # header with empty value; value part (val) after ; ignored
            headers.append((key, ''))
        elif sep == '@':
            # file upload for multipart
            path = val
            filename = None
            mimetype = None
            # Check for ;type= and ;filename=
            parts = path.split(';')
            path = parts[0]
            for p in parts[1:]:
                if p.startswith('type='):
                    mimetype = p[5:]
                elif p.startswith('filename='):
                    filename = p[9:]
            files.append((key, path, filename, mimetype))
        elif sep == '=@':
            # read value from file as string
            try:
                with open(val, 'r') as f:
                    val = f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                eprint(f"error: cannot open file '{val}': {e}")
                sys.exit(2)
            body.append((key, val, 'str'))
        elif sep == ':=@':
            # read value from file as JSON
            try:
                with open(val, 'r') as f:
                    parsed = jsonlib.load(f)
            except Exception:
                eprint(f"error: \"{item}\" is not a valid request item")
                sys.exit(2)
            body.append((key, parsed, 'json'))
    
    return headers, body, query, files


def build_json_body(body):
    obj = {}
    for k, v, t in body:
        # For now basic: just set key to value
        # Could support nested paths but complex
        obj[k] = v
    return jsonlib.dumps(obj, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)


def build_form_body(body):
    # x-www-form-urlencoded
    parts = []
    for k, v, t in body:
        if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
            v = jsonlib.dumps(v)
        elif v is True:
            v = "true"
        elif v is False:
            v = "false"
        elif v is None:
            v = "null"
        elif not isinstance(v, str):
            v = str(v)
        parts.append(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}")
    return '&'.join(parts)


def gen_boundary():
    parts = []
    for _ in range(4):
        parts.append(''.join(random.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(16)))
    return '-'.join(parts)


def build_multipart_body(body, files):
    boundary = gen_boundary()
    out = []
    crlf = "\r\n"
    for k, v, t in body:
        if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
            v = jsonlib.dumps(v)
        elif v is True:
            v = "true"
        elif v is False:
            v = "false"
        elif v is None:
            v = "null"
        else:
            v = str(v)
        out.append(f"--{boundary}\n")
        out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"\n\n")
        out.append(f"{v}\n")
    for k, path, filename, mimetype in files:
        fn = filename or os.path.basename(path)
        out.append(f"--{boundary}\n")
        if mimetype:
            out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"; filename=\"{fn}\"\n")
            out.append(f"Content-Type: {mimetype}\n\n")
        else:
            out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"; filename=\"{fn}\"\n\n")
        try:
            with open(path, 'rb') as f:
                out.append(f.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
        except OSError:
            pass
        out.append("\n")
    out.append(f"--{boundary}--\n")
    return boundary, ''.join(out)


def add_query(url, query_items):
    if not query_items:
        return url
    p = urlparse(url)
    existing = p.query
    new_q = '&'.join(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}" for k, v in query_items)
    if existing:
        combined = existing + '&' + new_q
    else:
        combined = new_q
    return urlunparse((p.scheme, p.netloc, p.path, p.params, combined, p.fragment))


def parse_basic_auth(auth_str):
    if ':' in auth_str:
        user, pw = auth_str.split(':', 1)
    else:
        user, pw = auth_str, ''
    creds = f"{user}:{pw}".encode()
    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(creds).decode()


def print_request_offline(args):
    url = normalize_url(args.url, https=args.https)
    parsed = urlparse(url)

    # Extract user:pass from URL
    url_user = None
    url_pass = None
    netloc = parsed.netloc
    if '@' in netloc:
        userinfo, _, hostpart = netloc.rpartition('@')
        if ':' in userinfo:
            url_user, url_pass = userinfo.split(':', 1)
        else:
            url_user, url_pass = userinfo, ''
        # Rebuild netloc without userinfo
        parsed = parsed._replace(netloc=hostpart)
        url = urlunparse(parsed)
    
    headers_raw, body, query, files = parse_request_items(args.items, 
        'json' if args.json else ('form' if args.form else 'multipart'))

    # Determine method
    method = args.method
    if method is None:
        if body or files or args.raw is not None:
            method = "POST"
        elif not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
            method = "POST"
        else:
            method = "GET"

    # Build the body
    body_bytes = b""
    content_type = None
    body_str = ""
    if args.raw is not None:
        body_str = args.raw
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        if args.json:
            content_type = "application/json"
        elif args.form:
            content_type = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    elif args.multipart or files:
        boundary, body_str = build_multipart_body(body, files)
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        content_type = f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"
    elif args.form:
        body_str = build_form_body(body)
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        if body:
            content_type = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    elif body:
        # JSON
        body_str = build_json_body(body)
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        content_type = "application/json"
    elif not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
        # Read from stdin
        body_bytes = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        body_str = body_bytes.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    
    # Check if stdin has data AND request data was provided
    # (Actually implemented as: stdin readable AND body items set)
    stdin_has_data = not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty()
    if stdin_has_data and (body or files or args.raw is not None):
        eprint(f"{PROG_NAME}: error: Request body (from stdin) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed. Pass --ignore-stdin to ignore standard input.")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Build path
    url_with_query = add_query(url, query)
    p = urlparse(url_with_query)
    path = p.path or "/"
    if p.query:
        path += "?" + p.query

    # Build headers
    # Determine defaults
    ordered_headers = []
    ordered_headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate, br, zstd"))
    ordered_headers.append(("User-Agent", f"xh/{VERSION}"))
    ordered_headers.append(("Connection", "keep-alive"))

    # Auth header from URL or --auth
    auth_header = None
    if args.auth is not None:
        if args.auth_type == "basic":
            auth_header = parse_basic_auth(args.auth)
        elif args.auth_type == "bearer":
            auth_header = "Bearer " + args.auth
    elif url_user is not None:
        auth_header = parse_basic_auth(f"{url_user}:{url_pass or ''}")

    # URL-auth goes between Accept-Encoding and User-Agent? No, actually from testing,
    # url auth appears right after the status line; --auth appears after Connection
    # Let's test: URL-auth comes as:
    #   Accept-Encoding
    #   User-Agent
    #   Connection
    # Wait no:  the URL auth was:
    #   GET /get HTTP/1.1
    #   Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz     <-- first
    #   Accept-Encoding...
    
    # For --auth: Authorization came after Connection.
    
    # Rebuild ordered headers correctly:
    final_headers = []
    if url_user is not None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    final_headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate, br, zstd"))
    final_headers.append(("User-Agent", f"xh/{VERSION}"))
    final_headers.append(("Connection", "keep-alive"))
    if args.auth is not None and url_user is None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    
    # User-specified headers come next
    user_headers = []
    removed = set()
    host_override = None
    for k, v in headers_raw:
        if v is None:

    #   Content-Type: application/xml   (user override)

    user_accept = None

    #   Accept-Encoding
    #   User-Agent
    #   Connection

    #   Content-Type: application/xml     <-- user-provided

    #   Accept-Encoding
    #   User-Agent

                eprint(usage_line())
                eprint()
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
        if a.startswith("--"):
            # Can be --opt or --opt=val
            if "=" in a:
                key, val = a[2:].split("=", 1)
            else:
                key = a[2:]
                val = None
            if key not in OPTION_DEFS:
                eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found")
                eprint()
                eprint("  tip: to pass '{}' as a value, use '-- {}'".format(a, a))
                eprint()
                eprint(usage_line())
                eprint()
                eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                sys.exit(2)
            short, takes_value, dest, is_multi = OPTION_DEFS[key]
            if takes_value:
                if val is None:
                    if i + 1 >= n:
                        vals = VALID_VALUES.get(key)
                        msg = f"error: a value is required for '--{key} <{key.upper().replace('-','_')}>' but none was supplied"
                        eprint(msg)
                        if vals:
                            eprint(f"  [possible values: {', '.join(vals)}]")
                        eprint()
                        eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                        sys.exit(2)
                    val = argv[i+1]
                    i += 1
            else:
                if val is not None:
                    eprint(f"error: unexpected value '{val}' for '--{key}' found; no more were expected")
                    eprint()
                    eprint(usage_line())
                    eprint()
                    eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
            set_arg(args, key, val)
            i += 1
            continue
        if a.startswith("-") and len(a) > 1 and not _is_negative_number(a):
            # Short option(s): -abc or -abvalue
            j = 1
            while j < len(a):
                ch = a[j]
                if ch not in SHORT_TO_LONG:
                    eprint(f"error: unexpected argument '-{ch}' found")
                    eprint()
                    eprint(usage_line())
                    eprint()
                    eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                    sys.exit(2)
                long = SHORT_TO_LONG[ch]
                short, takes_value, dest, is_multi = OPTION_DEFS[long]
                if takes_value:
                    # Rest of arg is value; else next arg
                    rest = a[j+1:]
                    if rest:
                        val = rest
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= n:
                            eprint(f"error: a value is required for '-{ch}' but none was supplied")
                            eprint()
                            eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
                            sys.exit(2)
                        val = argv[i+1]
                        i += 1
                    set_arg(args, long, val)
                    break
                else:
                    set_arg(args, long, None)
                    j += 1
            i += 1
            continue
        # Positional
        positional.append(a)
        i += 1

    # Parse positional args
    if not positional:
        eprint("error: the following required arguments were not provided:")
        eprint("  <[METHOD] URL>")
        eprint()
        eprint(f"Usage: {PROG_NAME} <[METHOD] URL> [REQUEST_ITEM]...")
        eprint()
        eprint("For more information, try '--help'.")
        sys.exit(2)

    # Handle 'help' subcommand-ish
    if positional[0] == "help" and len(positional) == 1:
        # Long help - just print short for now
        sys.stdout.write(short_help())
        sys.exit(0)

    # Determine method/URL
    first = positional[0]
    if len(positional) == 1:
        # Only one positional - it's URL (check if it's a valid URL or method-like)
        if is_method_like(first):
            # Looks like a method only
            make_error("Missing <URL>")
        args.method = None
        args.url = first
        rest = []
    else:
        if is_method_like(first):
            args.method = first.upper()
            args.url = positional[1]
            rest = positional[2:]
        else:
            args.method = None
            args.url = first
            rest = positional[1:]

    args.items = rest
    return args


def _is_negative_number(s):
    """Check if argument is a negative number (e.g. '-1'), not a flag."""
    if len(s) < 2 or s[0] != '-':
        return False
    return all(c.isdigit() or c == '.' for c in s[1:])


def normalize_url(url, https=False):
    """Normalize xh-style URL to proper URL.
    
    Rules:
    - Starts with http:// or https:// -> use as-is
    - Starts with ://  -> strip and prepend scheme
    - Starts with :PORT or :/ -> prepend localhost
    - Otherwise prepend scheme
    """
    scheme = "https" if https else "http"
    if url.startswith("://"):
        url = scheme + url
    elif url.startswith("http://") or url.startswith("https://"):
        pass
    elif url.startswith(":"):
        # localhost shorthand
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest == "" or rest.startswith("/"):
            # :/path -> localhost/path (but ":" alone is localhost:/)
            url = f"{scheme}://localhost{rest}"
        else:
            # :PORT/path -> localhost:PORT/path
            url = f"{scheme}://localhost:{rest}"
    else:
        url = f"{scheme}://{url}"
    return url


def parse_request_items(items, mode):
    """Parse items like key=val, key:=val, key==val, key:val, key;, file@path.
    
    mode: 'json', 'form', 'multipart'
    Returns:
      headers (list of (key, val) pairs; None val means unset)
      body_items (list of dicts)
      query_items (list of (key, val))
      files (for multipart)
    """
    headers = []
    body = []  # list of (key, value, type) where type in 'str','json','raw'
    query = []
    files = []  # list of (name, path, filename, mimetype)
    
    def unescape(s):
        # Handle escape sequences like \: or \= 
        out = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(s):
            if s[i] == '\\' and i + 1 < len(s):
                out.append(s[i+1])
                i += 2
            else:
                out.append(s[i])
                i += 1
        return ''.join(out)
    
    # Find unescaped separator - longer sep first
    SEPS = [':=@', ':=', '==', '=@', '@', '=', ':', ';']
    
    for item in items:
        # Find earliest unescaped separator, preferring longer
        best_idx = None
        best_sep = None
        i = 0
        while i < len(item):
            if item[i] == '\\':
                i += 2
                continue
            for sep in SEPS:
                if item[i:i+len(sep)] == sep:
                    if best_idx is None or i < best_idx or (i == best_idx and len(sep) > len(best_sep)):
                        best_idx = i
                        best_sep = sep
                    break
            i += 1
        
        if best_idx is None:
            # No separator
            eprint(f"error: \"{item}\" is not a valid request item")
            sys.exit(2)
        
        key = unescape(item[:best_idx])
        val = item[best_idx + len(best_sep):]
        
        sep = best_sep
        # @ prefix in value means read from file
        if sep in (':=', '=', ':', 'header'):
            if val.startswith('@'):
                path = val[1:]
                try:
                    with open(path, 'r') as f:
                        val = f.read()
                except OSError as e:
                    eprint(f"error: cannot open file '{path}': {e}")
                    sys.exit(2)
        
        if sep == ':=':
            # JSON value
            try:
                parsed = jsonlib.loads(val)
            except Exception:
                eprint(f"error: \"{item}\" is not a valid request item")
                sys.exit(2)
            body.append((key, parsed, 'json'))
        elif sep == '==':
            query.append((key, val))
        elif sep == '=':
            body.append((key, val, 'str'))
        elif sep == ':':
            if val == '':
                headers.append((key, None))  # unset
            else:
                headers.append((key, val))
        elif sep == ';':
            # header with empty value; value part (val) after ; ignored
            headers.append((key, ''))
        elif sep == '@':
            # file upload for multipart
            path = val
            filename = None
            mimetype = None
            # Check for ;type= and ;filename=
            parts = path.split(';')
            path = parts[0]
            for p in parts[1:]:
                if p.startswith('type='):
                    mimetype = p[5:]
                elif p.startswith('filename='):
                    filename = p[9:]
            files.append((key, path, filename, mimetype))
        elif sep == '=@':
            # read value from file as string
            try:
                with open(val, 'r') as f:
                    val = f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                eprint(f"error: cannot open file '{val}': {e}")
                sys.exit(2)
            body.append((key, val, 'str'))
        elif sep == ':=@':
            # read value from file as JSON
            try:
                with open(val, 'r') as f:
                    parsed = jsonlib.load(f)
            except Exception:
                eprint(f"error: \"{item}\" is not a valid request item")
                sys.exit(2)
            body.append((key, parsed, 'json'))
    
    return headers, body, query, files


def build_json_body(body):
    obj = {}
    for k, v, t in body:
        # For now basic: just set key to value
        # Could support nested paths but complex
        obj[k] = v
    return jsonlib.dumps(obj, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)


def build_form_body(body):
    # x-www-form-urlencoded
    parts = []
    for k, v, t in body:
        if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
            v = jsonlib.dumps(v)
        elif v is True:
            v = "true"
        elif v is False:
            v = "false"
        elif v is None:
            v = "null"
        elif not isinstance(v, str):
            v = str(v)
        parts.append(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}")
    return '&'.join(parts)


def gen_boundary():
    parts = []
    for _ in range(4):
        parts.append(''.join(random.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(16)))
    return '-'.join(parts)


def build_multipart_body(body, files):
    boundary = gen_boundary()
    out = []
    crlf = "\r\n"
    for k, v, t in body:
        if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
            v = jsonlib.dumps(v)
        elif v is True:
            v = "true"
        elif v is False:
            v = "false"
        elif v is None:
            v = "null"
        else:
            v = str(v)
        out.append(f"--{boundary}\n")
        out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"\n\n")
        out.append(f"{v}\n")
    for k, path, filename, mimetype in files:
        fn = filename or os.path.basename(path)
        out.append(f"--{boundary}\n")
        if mimetype:
            out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"; filename=\"{fn}\"\n")
            out.append(f"Content-Type: {mimetype}\n\n")
        else:
            out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"; filename=\"{fn}\"\n\n")
        try:
            with open(path, 'rb') as f:
                out.append(f.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
        except OSError:
            pass
        out.append("\n")
    out.append(f"--{boundary}--\n")
    return boundary, ''.join(out)


def add_query(url, query_items):
    if not query_items:
        return url
    p = urlparse(url)
    existing = p.query
    new_q = '&'.join(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}" for k, v in query_items)
    if existing:
        combined = existing + '&' + new_q
    else:
        combined = new_q
    return urlunparse((p.scheme, p.netloc, p.path, p.params, combined, p.fragment))


def parse_basic_auth(auth_str):
    if ':' in auth_str:
        user, pw = auth_str.split(':', 1)
    else:
        user, pw = auth_str, ''
    creds = f"{user}:{pw}".encode()
    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(creds).decode()


def print_request_offline(args):
    url = normalize_url(args.url, https=args.https)
    parsed = urlparse(url)

    # Extract user:pass from URL
    url_user = None
    url_pass = None
    netloc = parsed.netloc
    if '@' in netloc:
        userinfo, _, hostpart = netloc.rpartition('@')
        if ':' in userinfo:
            url_user, url_pass = userinfo.split(':', 1)
        else:
            url_user, url_pass = userinfo, ''
        # Rebuild netloc without userinfo
        parsed = parsed._replace(netloc=hostpart)
        url = urlunparse(parsed)
    
    headers_raw, body, query, files = parse_request_items(args.items, 
        'json' if args.json else ('form' if args.form else 'multipart'))

    # Determine method
    method = args.method
    if method is None:
        if body or files or args.raw is not None:
            method = "POST"
        elif not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
            method = "POST"
        else:
            method = "GET"

    # Build the body
    body_bytes = b""
    content_type = None
    body_str = ""
    if args.raw is not None:
        body_str = args.raw
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        if args.json:
            content_type = "application/json"
        elif args.form:
            content_type = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    elif args.multipart or files:
        boundary, body_str = build_multipart_body(body, files)
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        content_type = f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"
    elif args.form:
        body_str = build_form_body(body)
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        if body:
            content_type = "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
    elif body:
        # JSON
        body_str = build_json_body(body)
        body_bytes = body_str.encode('utf-8')
        content_type = "application/json"
    elif not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
        # Read from stdin
        body_bytes = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        body_str = body_bytes.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    
    # Check if stdin has data AND request data was provided
    # (Actually implemented as: stdin readable AND body items set)
    stdin_has_data = not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty()
    if stdin_has_data and (body or files or args.raw is not None):
        eprint(f"{PROG_NAME}: error: Request body (from stdin) and request data (key=value) cannot be mixed. Pass --ignore-stdin to ignore standard input.")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Build path
    url_with_query = add_query(url, query)
    p = urlparse(url_with_query)
    path = p.path or "/"
    if p.query:
        path += "?" + p.query

    # Build headers
    # Determine defaults
    ordered_headers = []
    ordered_headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate, br, zstd"))
    ordered_headers.append(("User-Agent", f"xh/{VERSION}"))
    ordered_headers.append(("Connection", "keep-alive"))

    # Auth header from URL or --auth
    auth_header = None
    if args.auth is not None:
        if args.auth_type == "basic":
            auth_header = parse_basic_auth(args.auth)
        elif args.auth_type == "bearer":
            auth_header = "Bearer " + args.auth
    elif url_user is not None:
        auth_header = parse_basic_auth(f"{url_user}:{url_pass or ''}")

    # URL-auth goes between Accept-Encoding and User-Agent? No, actually from testing,
    # url auth appears right after the status line; --auth appears after Connection
    # Let's test: URL-auth comes as:
    #   Accept-Encoding
    #   User-Agent
    #   Connection
    # Wait no:  the URL auth was:
    #   GET /get HTTP/1.1
    #   Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz     <-- first
    #   Accept-Encoding...
    
    # For --auth: Authorization came after Connection.
    
    # Rebuild ordered headers correctly:
    final_headers = []
    if url_user is not None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    final_headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate, br, zstd"))
    final_headers.append(("User-Agent", f"xh/{VERSION}"))
    final_headers.append(("Connection", "keep-alive"))
    if args.auth is not None and url_user is None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    
    # User-specified headers come next
    user_headers = []
    removed = set()
    host_override = None
    for k, v in headers_raw:
        if v is None:
            removed.add(k.lower())
        else:
            if k.lower() == 'host':
                host_override = v
            else:
                user_headers.append((k, v))
    for k, v in user_headers:
        final_headers.append((normalize_header_name(k), v))
    
    # Content-Type logic - how to insert it?
    # Test showed: when there are user headers like x-header: foo,
    # the user headers appear BEFORE Accept. When no user headers, Accept comes right after Connection.
    # Content-Type appears after Accept.
    # But when x-header exists: user header before Accept. Let me re-read the output:
    #   POST /post HTTP/1.1
    #   Accept-Encoding: ...
    #   User-Agent: ...
    #   Connection: keep-alive
    #   X-Header: foo
    #   Y-Header: bar
    #   Accept: */*
    # vs with body:
    #   Accept-Encoding, User-Agent, Connection
    #   Accept: application/json, */*;q=0.5
    #   Content-Type: application/json
    #   Content-Length: 25
    # and with both user headers AND body from my test:
    #   Accept-Encoding, User-Agent, Connection
    #   Accept: application/json, */*;q=0.5
    #   Content-Type: application/xml   (user override)
    #   foo header would be after...
    
    # Reorder: put user headers right after Connection, then Accept, then Content-Type, then Content-Length.
    # But we also need to preserve the observed behavior: when Content-Type is user-set it replaces the default.
    
    # Reset and rebuild final_headers properly
    final_headers = []
    if url_user is not None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    final_headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate, br, zstd"))
    final_headers.append(("User-Agent", f"xh/{VERSION}"))
    final_headers.append(("Connection", "keep-alive"))
    if args.auth is not None and url_user is None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    
    # User-specified headers (excluding special content-type, accept, host)
    user_ct = None
    user_accept = None
    other_user = []
    for k, v in user_headers:
        kl = k.lower()
        if kl == 'content-type':
            user_ct = v
        elif kl == 'accept':
            user_accept = v
        else:
            other_user.append((normalize_header_name(k), v))
    
    # Based on observations:
    # With body/multipart/form, default Accept is application/json,...
    # With GET/no body, default Accept is */*
    # If user sets x-header, it comes BEFORE Accept unless there's no body
    # Test: `httpbin.org Content-Type:application/xml foo=bar` produces:
    #   Accept-Encoding
    #   User-Agent
    #   Connection
    #   Accept: application/json, */*;q=0.5
    #   Content-Type: application/xml     <-- user-provided
    #   Content-Length
    # In this case there's no other_user header after Accept. But in the other test:
    # `post httpbin.org/post x-header:foo y-header:bar` produces:
    #   Accept-Encoding
    #   User-Agent  
    #   Connection
    #   X-Header: foo
    #   Y-Header: bar
    #   Accept: */*
    # So user headers appear BEFORE Accept when no body... hmm that's weird.
    # But in both cases, Accept follows after user headers, and Content-Type is right after Accept.
    
    # Actually what's going on: user headers are in order, then at insertion point where defaults go: Accept, Content-Type, Content-Length, Host.
    # Let's go with: Accept-Encoding, User-Agent, Connection, [user_headers], Accept, Content-Type, Content-Length, Host
    # And for user-supplied Accept and Content-Type, they REPLACE the default.

    for k, v in other_user:
        final_headers.append((k, v))
    
    # Accept header
    if user_accept is not None:
        accept_val = user_accept
    else:
        if args.json and (body or args.raw is not None and args.json):
            accept_val = "application/json, */*;q=0.5"
        elif body or args.raw is not None:
            # form or multipart
            accept_val = "*/*"
        else:
            accept_val = "*/*"
    # When JSON mode without body items (e.g. GET), accept should be */*
    # From testing: --offline httpbin.org alone: Accept: */*
    # With body items: Accept: application/json, */*;q=0.5
    if args.json and (body or args.raw is not None) and user_accept is None:
        accept_val = "application/json, */*;q=0.5"
    final_headers.append(("Accept", accept_val))
    
    # Content-Type
    if user_ct is not None:
        final_headers.append(("Content-Type", user_ct))
    elif content_type is not None:
        final_headers.append(("Content-Type", content_type))
    
    # Content-Length
    has_body_ct = (user_ct is not None) or (content_type is not None) or method in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH")
    if method in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH") or body_bytes:
        final_headers.append(("Content-Length", str(len(body_bytes))))
    
    # Host
    host = host_override
    if host is None:
        host = p.hostname or ""
        if p.port:
            host = f"{host}:{p.port}"
    final_headers.append(("Host", host))
    
    # Print request
    out = []
    out.append(f"{method} {path} HTTP/1.1")
    for k, v in final_headers:
        out.append(f"{k}: {v}")
    out.append("")
    if body_str:
        out.append(body_str)
    out.append("")
    if args.multipart or files or body_bytes:
        out.append("")
    print('\n'.join(out))


def normalize_header_name(k):
    """Normalize header name: lowercase then title-case each word (x-header -> X-Header)."""
    parts = k.split('-')
    return '-'.join(p[:1].upper() + p[1:].lower() if p else p for p in parts)


def print_curl(args):
    url = normalize_url(args.url, https=args.https)
    parsed = urlparse(url)

    # Extract userinfo
    url_user = None
    url_pass = None
    netloc = parsed.netloc
    if '@' in netloc:
        userinfo, _, hostpart = netloc.rpartition('@')
        if ':' in userinfo:
            url_user, url_pass = userinfo.split(':', 1)
        else:
            url_user, url_pass = userinfo, ''
        parsed = parsed._replace(netloc=hostpart)
        url = urlunparse(parsed)
    
    headers_raw, body, query, files = parse_request_items(args.items,
        'json' if args.json else ('form' if args.form else 'multipart'))
    
    url_with_query = add_query(url, query)
    
    method = args.method
    if method is None:
        if body or files or args.raw is not None:
            method = "POST"
        elif not args.ignore_stdin and not sys.stdin.isatty():
            method = "POST"
        else:
            method = "GET"
    
    cmd = ["curl"]
    if method != "GET":
        cmd.append("-X" if not args.curl_long else "--request")
        cmd.append(method)
    cmd.append(url_with_query)
    
    # Content-Type etc
    body_str = None
    if args.raw is not None:
        body_str = args.raw
        if args.json:
            cmd.append("-H" if not args.curl_long else "--header")
            cmd.append("content-type: application/json")
        elif args.form:
            cmd.append("-H" if not args.curl_long else "--header")
            cmd.append("content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    elif args.multipart or files:
        # Use -F for each
        for k, v, t in body:
            cmd.append("-F" if not args.curl_long else "--form")
            cmd.append(f"{k}={v}")
        for k, path, filename, mimetype in files:
            fn = f"@{path}"
            cmd.append("-F" if not args.curl_long else "--form")
            cmd.append(f"{k}={fn}")
    elif args.form and body:
        body_str = build_form_body(body)
        cmd.append("-H" if not args.curl_long else "--header")
        cmd.append("content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    elif body:
        body_str = build_json_body(body)
        cmd.append("-H" if not args.curl_long else "--header")
        cmd.append("content-type: application/json")
        cmd.append("-H" if not args.curl_long else "--header")
        cmd.append("accept: application/json, */*;q=0.5")
    
    for k, v in headers_raw:

    - Starts with :PORT or :/ -> prepend localhost
    - Otherwise prepend scheme

    scheme = "https" if https else "http"
    if url.startswith("://"):

    elif url.startswith("http://") or url.startswith("https://"):

    elif url.startswith(":"):
        # localhost shorthand
        rest = url[1:]
        if rest == "" or rest.startswith("/"):
            # :/path -> localhost/path (but ":" alone is localhost:/)
            url = f"{scheme}://localhost{rest}"
        else:
            # :PORT/path -> localhost:PORT/path
            url = f"{scheme}://localhost:{rest}"
    else:
        url = f"{scheme}://{url}"

            else:

            headers.append((key, ''))

            mimetype = None

def build_json_body(body):
    obj = {}
    for k, v, t in body:
        # For now basic: just set key to value
        # Could support nested paths but complex
        obj[k] = v
    return jsonlib.dumps(obj, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False)


def build_form_body(body):
    # x-www-form-urlencoded
    parts = []
    for k, v, t in body:
        if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
            v = jsonlib.dumps(v)
        elif v is True:
            v = "true"
        elif v is False:
            v = "false"
        elif v is None:
            v = "null"
        elif not isinstance(v, str):
            v = str(v)
        parts.append(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}")
    return '&'.join(parts)


def gen_boundary():
    parts = []
    for _ in range(4):
        parts.append(''.join(random.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(16)))
    return '-'.join(parts)


def build_multipart_body(body, files):
    boundary = gen_boundary()
    out = []
    crlf = "\r\n"
    for k, v, t in body:
        if isinstance(v, (dict, list)):
            v = jsonlib.dumps(v)
        elif v is True:
            v = "true"
        elif v is False:
            v = "false"
        elif v is None:
            v = "null"
        else:
            v = str(v)
        out.append(f"--{boundary}\n")
        out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"\n\n")
        out.append(f"{v}\n")
    for k, path, filename, mimetype in files:
        fn = filename or os.path.basename(path)
        out.append(f"--{boundary}\n")
        if mimetype:
            out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"; filename=\"{fn}\"\n")
            out.append(f"Content-Type: {mimetype}\n\n")
        else:
            out.append(f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{k}\"; filename=\"{fn}\"\n\n")
        try:
            with open(path, 'rb') as f:
                out.append(f.read().decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
        except OSError:
            pass
        out.append("\n")
    out.append(f"--{boundary}--\n")
    return boundary, ''.join(out)


def add_query(url, query_items):
    if not query_items:
        return url
    p = urlparse(url)
    existing = p.query
    new_q = '&'.join(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}" for k, v in query_items)
    if existing:
        combined = existing + '&' + new_q
    else:
        combined = new_q
    return urlunparse((p.scheme, p.netloc, p.path, p.params, combined, p.fragment))


def parse_basic_auth(auth_str):
    if ':' in auth_str:
        user, pw = auth_str.split(':', 1)
    else:
        user, pw = auth_str, ''
    creds = f"{user}:{pw}".encode()
    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(creds).decode()

    #   Content-Type: application/xml   (user override)
    #   foo header would be after...
    
    # Reorder: put user headers right after Connection, then Accept, then Content-Type, then Content-Length.

    # Reset and rebuild final_headers properly
    final_headers = []
    if url_user is not None:
        final_headers.append(("Authorization", auth_header))
    final_headers.append(("Accept-Encoding", "gzip, deflate, br, zstd"))
    final_headers.append(("User-Agent", f"xh/{VERSION}"))

    if args.auth is not None and url_user is None:

    # User-specified headers (excluding special content-type, accept, host)
    user_ct = None
    user_accept = None
    other_user = []
    for k, v in user_headers:

    for k, v in other_user:

    """Normalize header name: lowercase then title-case each word (x-header -> X-Header)."""

def shell_quote_cmd(cmd):
    out = []
    for c in cmd:
        if c == '' or any(ch in c for ch in ' \t\n"\'`$&|<>()[]{}*?#;\\') or '=' in c[1:]:
            # Use single quote
            if "'" in c:
                out.append('"' + c.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"').replace('$', '\\$') + '"')
            else:
                out.append("'" + c + "'")
        elif re.match(r'^[A-Za-z0-9_\-./:@%+]+$', c):
            out.append(c)
        else:
            out.append("'" + c + "'")
    return ' '.join(out)

SHORT_TO_LONG = {}
